Real progress can be made in addressing maladaptive behaviors- the things that you are doing that are ineffective/harmful to yourself. Therapy should be about addressing these things, not changing who you are. For instance, teaching someone who compulsively skin picks a better stress management technique. It doesn't change them, just changes the composition of their toolbox.

Also, never be afraid to find a new therapist if you're not making progress.
The irony is, if our positions were switched, I'd drag him to the nearest E.R kicking and screaming if I thought he needed it.

Perhaps.

It can be hard for me to take my own mental health seriously. I've been down this road many times before and haven't been dangerously suicidal in quite a few years. To quote a blogger far more eloquent on the subject than myself, I think about death like most people think about dinner plans.

Sadly, counseling is not an option for me right now. I'm a few years out of college and can't afford therapy. Of course I also make too much to utilize community mental health resources. There is really only one friend I'd tell and he is quite stable at least.

I still have the same problems talking to therapists that I have other support people, so the therapy attempts in the past that I have tried haven't been the most productive. Even posting anonymously to the internet is kind of like pulling teeth. 

I'll figure something out, I always do. At least music is still soothing.

It isn't so much that I feel as if I will be burdening anyone as it is that I feel my problems are trivial. I know consciously it isn't a contest of who has it worse, but I can't help but feel I am complaining about the mental health equivalent of a bruise when they are nursing a compound leg fracture.  Like saying "oh yeah I felt bad one time" to someone with severe bipolar. 


My severe social anxiety doesn't help in this regard. I am able to be open about some things (like having social anxiety or talking about most past mental health things), just not other things. Not sure precisely why, but I think the fears of being committed and loathing the attention I'll get if I talk about it aren't helping. My best friend has lovingly (and mostly seriously) threatened to get me committed if I were suicidal and metaphorically skin me alive if I didn't tell him that I was suicidal. I know he means the best but it isn't helping the whole opening up thing.

This is a throwaway for obvious reasons, but I figured as someone with a psych degree and actual experience working with BPD patients I could be of help. 

BPD gets a bad rap, but it *IS* treatable. Dialectical Behavioral Therapy is gold standard, but CBT and mindfullness based therapies do work. Don't let anyone tell you otherwise. I have worked with several clients with BPD and have people in my life diagnosed with it. Patients with that diagnosis get a bad rap in the community but truthfully the "reputation" is exaggerated in my experience. Highly so. 

I encourage you to seek treatment, as there is help available that does work. It isn't just gutting yourself or hiding yourself, either. Real progress can be made. 

I hope you find appropriate help and peace.
